text:
People ask how warm the sea is today.
Water temperature?
Is the sea cold?
How warm is the water at the beach?
I'm on the sofa planning a trip to the beach, so is the sea warm enough to swim in?
Tell me the sea temperature, please.
Will I freeze if I jump in?
I paid for a whole day on the sand, and I'd like to know if the water is warm enough for the kids.
Could you please check the water temperature near the pier? I'd like to know before we drive there.

A coffee order is a small set of choices. You pick the drink, the size, how strong it is and how sweet. A coffee machine or a smart kettle at home lets you change the same things. People say make it stronger, less milk, or just one sugar. Tea works the same way: weaker, hotter, no honey. Some choices are temporary, like extra ice on one hot day, and some stay for good, like always using oat milk. Friends may laugh when someone orders a tiny cup with five sugars, but it is their cup. A smoothie can be thicker or thinner, and someone with a bottle in a pocket might say, fill it with a cold, sweet one.

Bo ran a small hardware shop and wanted to know why the power bill was so high. Between customers, a delivery truck backed up outside, and Bo typed on the phone in a hurry: show me how mush power the shop used this week. The assistant opened the energy report and said the shop had used 310 units, mostly from the freezer and the lights at night. Bo asked it to filter the list to show only the evenings. The assistant did that, and now the chart showed a shallow dip at six and a big bump from the shop sign. Bo asked it to switch the sign off after closing. The assistant set a timer for every evening at seven and said it was done.

When you order food for delivery, the app shows the shop, the dishes, the price and a time. The time is a guess, and it moves when the shop is busy or the road is full. You can change a few things: add a note, pick a place to leave the bag, or give the rider a tip. People say leave it at the door, no onions please, or add a bigger tip. A rider might carry the bag on one arm or in a black box on the back of a bike. If the food is late, you can say where is my order, and the app shows the rider on a map. If you change your mind, say cancel it before the shop starts cooking.

Callum had just moved to the city and knew nobody, so he joined a monthly board game night at a cafe. His budget was small, so he did not buy a game. The host asked who could keep score, and Callum took out his phone and typed fast: keep scor for four players. The assistant made a score sheet with four names and said it would add up every round. Later, someone asked who should deal first. Callum said, shuffle the names and pick one. The assistant shuffled the list and chose Maya. Everyone laughed, and Callum felt a little less new in the city.

Olena was a retired teacher who liked to bake on Sundays. Her muffin recipe made fifteen muffins, but five neighbours were coming and she wanted three batches. She asked her phone, 'What is fifteen times three?' Before it answered, she tried to guess, and she said forty. The assistant said the answer was forty-five. 'And if I share them between five neighbours?' she asked. The assistant said nine each. Olena wrote nine on a note next to the first ingredient on her list, which was eggs, and went to find the big bowl.

Tessa was not good with technology, but her grandson Leo had put a puzzle app on her tablet. This morning it would not open. 'Please help, the puzzle is stuck,' she told the speaker. The assistant said the tablet was offline and walked her through joining the home wifi, one step at a time. The puzzle opened at once. Tessa had only watched one episode of her show that day, so she felt she had time to play. Then she said, 'Remind me to play with Leo the day after tomorrow at five.' The assistant said the reminder was set for Thursday at five. Tessa went to brush her hair, pleased with herself, while the puzzle waited on the table.

Aroha was in a hurry. Guests were coming in an hour, and the kitchen floor was in a serious mess. She called out to the robot vacuum, 'Clean the whole kitchen and the hall now!' The small camera on the robot looked around the room, and the assistant said it had started and would take about forty minutes. Aroha was slicing lemons for the drinks and said, 'That's too long. Just the kitchen, please.' The assistant changed the job to the kitchen only and said it would take twelve minutes. 'Tell me when it's done,' said Aroha. When the floor was clean, the assistant said the robot had cleaned about two hundred square feet and was going back to its dock.

Liam came home after a night shift, still in his work shirt, and dropped onto the sofa. His phone buzzed again and again. 'Why is it so loud?' he said. 'Turn off the notifications for the photo app for a few hours.' The assistant said it had paused them until noon, and that this was only temporary. Liam yawned and asked, 'How many new likes on my cat photo?' The assistant said thirty-one, but the page would not load the comments because the signal was weak. 'Try again in a minute,' said Liam. It tried again and read out two nice comments. He smiled, put the phone face down and went to sleep.

name: scale_recipe
does: This tool changes the amounts in a recipe for a new number of servings, like how many eggs to crack for a bigger cake.
inputs: the recipe, how many servings it makes now, and how many you want to make at home
people say:
- Make this recipe for six people
- I need double the pancakes
- There are only two of us tonight, can you halve it?
- How much flour for ten servings?
- Cut the cookie recipe down to a third

The router is the small box that sends the internet around your home. It is for sharing one connection with your phone, your laptop and the tv. People change the password, the name of the network, and who can join. When things are slow, they say restart the router or why is the wifi so slow. For visitors, many people ask for a guest network, so friends can join without seeing everything else. Some routers show how much data each device uses, and if the bill goes up by a dollar or two, people look at their plan. When the last device finally connects, everyone can cheer. If a page is stuck, people say try again or check the connection.

Chioma was packing the car for a weekend in the hills. The sky looked grey and she was already late. She put a pen and a small notebook in her bag and spoke to her phone: is it safe to hike tmorrow, any rain? The assistant said there would be light rain in the morning and clear skies after two, and that the trail by the river was safe after noon. Chioma asked it to make a packing list for one night. The assistant gave her a tent, a sleeping bag, water, a torch and a warm jacket. She touched each thing as she put it in the car, and then she drove off.

Siti owned a small shop that sold plants. One evening the main computer in her office was slow, and the screen was full of open files. Her pea plants waited by the window, a fly buzzed around the lamp, and she still had a customer list to print. She said to the assistant on her laptop, 'Could you please close the programs I am not using and restart the computer? I need it to be quick, because I have to print the orders before the shop opens tomorrow.' The assistant closed six windows, reminded her to save the list, and then restarted the computer. After two minutes it was fast again, and Siti printed the orders.

Many board games use a timer and a score. The timer sets how long each player has to move, and the score shows who is ahead. People change the time, add a player, or start over. They say set a two minute timer, add ten for Sam, or what is the score. In a quiet game, a player might lift a card and read a secret message aloud, so the group asks the assistant to keep the score for them. Some puzzles have a narrow path, and a timer makes it more exciting. If a rule is unclear, people ask can I do that, and the assistant reads the rule out loud.

People want to know how far they walked today.
how far did i walk todya
Distance?
How far have I gone since this morning?
What is my walking distance so far?
Can you convert my steps into miles? I want to know how far that is.
I was listening to an album and lost track of the walk, so how far did I go?
It was a difficult hill, so please tell me the total distance I covered.

Walter was a busy parent, and the kids wanted a game before dinner. 'Start a ten minute timer for hide and seek,' he told the speaker. A moment later he said, 'No, make it five, dinner is almost ready.' The assistant changed it to five minutes and counted down out loud. Little Mia hid behind a gray curtain, and Theo crouched by a pot with a flower in it. When time was up, the assistant said, 'Time's up!' and the kids came running out. Walter asked the assistant to forward the final score to Grandma, and it sent her a short text with the numbers.

When you write, the computer helps with spelling, word counts and editing. A word count tells you how long a text is, which matters when a school or a job sets a maximum. People ask how many words is this, check my spelling, or make it shorter. A voice tool can type what you say, and you may need to unmute the microphone first. Some laptops have a sensor that dims the screen at night, so reading and writing feel easier. When editing, people say undo that, read it back to me, or change tired to sleepy. A draft is only the first try, so changing it again is normal.

Plants need water, light and a bit of care. A sprinkler gives water on a timer, so you do not have to stand in the garden with a hose. People change how long it runs, which days, and how much water the soil gets. They say water the tomatoes for ten minutes, skip tomorrow, or continue the schedule next week. Seeds often start in a small pot or a jar on a sunny window. Good soil feels soft and smooth, and a finger test tells you if it is dry. When weeds come, people ask for a reminder to pull them each Saturday.

Samir, a retired teacher, had a new robot mower for his small garden. On Tuesday morning he told the assistant, 'Mow the lawn at ten.' Then he remembered his trip to the pharmacy and said, 'Sorry, I mean two o'clock, I will be out.' The assistant changed the time to two. Leaves had started to fall from the oak tree, so he added, 'And skip the edges today, the leaves are everywhere.' The assistant said the mower would cut only the middle. When Samir came home, the grass looked even and neat, and he was glad he had checked.

name: share_album
does: Sends a photo album to friends or family, so they know which pictures to look at, and it is most useful after a trip or a class party.
inputs: which album, who to send it to, and whether they can add their own photos
people say:
- Send the beach pictures to Mum
- Share my holiday photos with the group
- Let Ben see the birthday album
- Can my sister look at the pictures from the weekend?
- Show the class photos to everyone in the family

name: check_door_cameras
does: Shows what a camera at your door saw lately, so you can look even while you are out eating noodles at your favorite cafe, and talk to whoever is there.
inputs: which door, and how far back to look
people say:
- Did anyone come to the front door?
- Show me the back garden camera
- Who rang the bell an hour ago?
- Has my parcel arrived?
- Is someone at the gate?

Agnieszka had been in the garden all morning when her daughter called to say the little one had a cough. She asked the assistant, 'Please book a doctor's visit for Tuesday at nine.' Then she corrected herself: 'No, Wednesday, my daughter works on Tuesday.' The assistant booked Wednesday at nine and said it would send a reminder a few minutes before. Agnieszka asked, 'Can you boost the volume on that reminder so I hear it outside?' The assistant raised the alert sound. Then she went back to her roses, and her phone chimed loudly on the day.

name: baby_sleep_log
does: Writes down when the baby falls asleep and when she wakes, so a parent can see the pattern even from a remote room, and the house can stay quiet at nap time.
inputs: the baby's name, and whether she is asleep or awake
people say:
- The baby just fell asleep
- She is awake again
- When did he last nap?
- How long did she sleep this afternoon?
- Write down that the baby woke up at three

Person: Start my morning workout, please.
Assistant: Which one? Arms, legs, or the full body?
Person: Legs. Actually, no, make it the full body. The kids are asleep, so keep it quiet.
Assistant: Full body it is. Twenty minutes, quiet moves only. Shall I dim the lights?
Person: Yes, please dim them a bit. And play my favourite song.
Assistant: I can't play music, I'm sorry. I can count your sets and rests, though.
Person: That's fine. Maybe we can jog by the lake on Saturday.
Assistant: I can't plan outdoor routes, but I can set a reminder for Saturday morning.

Sipho had just moved to the city, and he had invited a neighbour to dinner. His best shirt was dirty. The laundry room was dark because the blind was down, so he turned on the light and asked the assistant, 'How long does a quick wash take? Can I use half the soap? It's my personal favourite shirt and I don't want to ruin it.' The assistant said a quick wash took thirty minutes, and half a cap of soap was plenty for a small load. Sipho started the machine and asked it to tell him when it was finished. Forty minutes later, the phone chimed, and the shirt was ready.

Mei's grandson Kai had started his first job, and he wanted to tell her about his first salary. Mei could not hear well, so she said to her phone, 'Call Kai and put it on speaker.' It rang, but Kai did not answer. 'Leave him a message,' said Mei. 'Say I will visit on the twelfth of March.' The assistant left the message. 'Mark that day on my calendar,' she added, and the assistant marked the date and said it would remind her a few days before. Mei sat back in her chair and waited for him to call, with a cup of tea.

Tessa, a student, found a thin cat on the stairs. It wore a tiny red dress that someone had made for it. She asked the assistant, 'Is anyone near me missing a cat?' It looked at the local notice board and found a post from a neighbour called Mr Lee, who had lost his cat Pepper four days ago. The post said Pepper liked a daily walk in the yard. 'Tell him I have the cat and I'll feed it until he comes,' said Tessa. The assistant sent the message. Mr Lee answered in a minute and said he would be there at six, and Tessa poured some milk into a bowl.

name: speaker_tips
does: Answers questions about what the speaker can do, like a search engine for its own features.
inputs: the feature you wonder about, such as volume, voices or playing in two rooms
people say:
- What can you do?
- Can you play in the kitchen and the bedroom together?
- Keep the sound low at night, can you do that?
- How do I change your voice?
- I wonder if you can read my messages

People want the speaker to play music louder.
Turn it up
A bit louder, please
I can barely hear the song in here
It's Saturday and the party is getting going, can you make the music louder?
Do you know how to make it louder? The damp towels in the dryer are drowning it out.
Could you raise the volume? I'd like everyone in the garden to hear it.
It's too quiet for dancing

People want to know when the baby last ate.
When was the last feed?
What time did she eat, and when can she eat again?
How long since the baby had milk?
I need an easy answer: when was the last bottle?
Unlock my phone and tell me when he last ate.
Show me the feeding log, I was at the shop counting coins and lost track.
Could you please tell me when the little one last had milk, and when the next feed is due?

Lerato came home after a night shift, tired but wanting to move a little. The day was mild, and the window by the vent was open. She told the speaker, 'Give me a quick workout, six exercises, nothing hard.' The assistant listed six: squats, push-ups, lunges, a plank, sit-ups and jumping jacks, with thirty seconds of rest in between. 'Remind me to fill my water bottle first,' she said. The assistant set the reminder for right then. Lerato filled the bottle, laid out her mat, and said, 'Start.' The assistant counted every set out loud until she was done.

People want the total of two numbers, even when they mix small and big ones.
what is 14 plus 9
14 + 9?
wat is 23 plus 18
Put 48 and 27 together
Could you tell me the sum of 48 and 27? I'm checking the bill when I get back tonight.
How much is it if I have 31 and then get 15 more?
Total of 12, 8 and 5
Please help me add up my receipts, which are 6.50 and 3.25.

Ethan was eight and going camping with his dad. He had read an article about the stars, and he wanted to see them. 'Weather tonight?' he asked the tablet. The assistant said it would be clear and cold. 'Make a list,' said Ethan. The assistant created a packing list with a tent, a sleeping bag, a torch and warm socks. Ethan read it to his dad. At the campsite, the little lamp in the tent was automatic and turned on when it got dark. Ethan lay on his back and counted the stars until he fell asleep.

Esteban was texting his friend while he helped with dinner. He typed to the assistant, 'my mom's recipe says two cups of flour but my scale only shows grams.' The assistant said two cups of flour was about 250 grams. Esteban poured flour into the bowl until the scale said 250, then he tossed the empty bag in the bin. He still had to pack lunch for his daily bike trip to school, so he asked, 'Remind me at eight to pack a lunch.' The assistant said it would remind him at eight. The bread smelled great by nine.

Henry was a student who wanted to bake his first loaf of bread. At the market he bought flour and yeast. The bag of flour held two thousand grams, and he asked the assistant, 'How many loaves can I make with this?' The assistant said about four. 'How long should bread be cooked, and how hot should the oven be?' The assistant said forty minutes at two hundred degrees. Henry set the oven and asked for a timer. The assistant started a forty minute timer. When it rang, the bread was golden and the whole flat smelled like a bakery.

Writing a letter or a report goes better in small steps. First you draft, then you check the spelling, then you edit. A word count helps when a teacher or boss wants a certain length. People ask how many words, fix the spelling, or make this sound more polite. If your hand is sore from typing, you can talk and let the computer write for you. A saved draft can notify you when someone else changes it. Some people keep a can of pens on the desk and write their ideas on paper first. When a sentence feels long, people say split it in two or shorter, please.

A social media page shows posts, likes and followers. People use it to share news with friends and to see what others are doing. They can change who sees a post, how many alerts they get, and what shows up first. They say turn off alerts, double check who can see this, or hide that post. A busy day can fill the phone with noise, so many people choose calm hours at night. After a good photo, followers can grow by a quarter in a week, and people ask how many new ones they have. To keep things private, they say make my account private.

Ovens, kettles and coffee machines are for heat and time. You choose a number, and the machine does the rest. An oven needs a temperature and minutes, a kettle needs to boil, and a dishwasher needs a wash mode. People say preheat to 180, boil the water, or start the quick wash. A recipe is like a document that lists exact amounts, so people calculate when they cook for more guests. If the oven is too hot, they say lower it by ten. A timer rings when the food is ready, and people say stop the timer when their hands are full.

name: resume_episode
does: Starts a podcast or audiobook again where you stopped, so you can divide a heavy book over many days.
inputs: which show or book, such as the one your uncle gave you
people say:
- Where did I stop in my book?
- Keep going with the story
- Continue my podcast
- Play the last episode from where I left it
- Start the audiobook again from yesterday

Edward was texting his cousin in Sydney while drawing in his notebook. He wondered if it was late there, so he asked the assistant, 'What time is it in Sydney?' The assistant said Sydney was ten hours ahead, so it was almost midnight. 'That's more than I thought,' said Edward. He decided not to call. The lamp was too bright for drawing, so he said, 'Dim my lamp by half.' The assistant dimmed it to half. 'And wake me at seven, double volume,' he added. The assistant set the alarm for seven and made it louder than usual.

Tendai's family was having a pool party, and his favorite cousin was coming. He typed quickly in lowercase: is the pool warm enuf for tomorrow. The assistant said the water was twenty-four degrees and would get warmer with the sun. 'Heat it up to twenty-seven,' typed Tendai. The assistant turned on the heater and said the pool would be ready by morning. Later in the evening, Tendai touched the water with his toe and found it already warmer. He told the assistant to cover the pool for the night, and the cover rolled across the water.

Person: Hello, could you please tell me the tyre pressure of my car? I'm driving to see my mother tomorrow and I'd like to be safe.
Assistant: Of course. Which car, the blue one or the white one?
Person: The blue one. It's silly, but I forgot to check last week.
Assistant: The front tyres read thirty-two and the back ones read thirty.
Person: Thanks. Can you fold in the mirrors? The car is in a narrow spot.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't control the mirrors.
Person: OK. I also saw a scratch in the paint. Can you book a repair?
Assistant: I can't book repairs, but I can remind you to call the garage.

name: heat_budget
does: Shows how much heating costs per day, so a family or a small class can afford to keep rooms warm without making them too hot.
inputs: which room or heater, and how many hours it is on
people say:
- How much does the heater cost per day?
- Can we afford to keep it on all night?
- Is it too expensive to heat the living room?
- What's my heating bill this week?
- Tell me what the radiator costs to run

When you buy something online, you get a number to track the parcel. The store sends an invoice, and the courier shows where the parcel is. People check when it will arrive, change the address, or ask for their money back. They say where is my parcel, change delivery to my work, or I'd like a refund. Mild problems, like a small delay, usually fix themselves. If something is broken, people think about returning it and ask how to send it back. Delivery times are only guesses, so they can move by a day.

Person: Good morning. I would like to see how much I spent on stock this month, please, because I need to decide if I can hire some help.
Assistant: Sure. Do you mean this month so far, or the last full month?
Person: This month so far.
Assistant: You spent 1,240 on stock. The shop is in the black, with 380 left after bills.
Person: Good. I want to build a savings plan. Can you move 100 into my savings?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't move money. I can set a reminder for the first of each month.
Person: Please do. And add 20 for the rope I bought for the sign.

Fatima was tired after a long day. Thunder rolled outside while the children did their homework. 'Could you please tell me when the electricity bill is due? I want to pay before the late fee, because money is tight this month.' The assistant said it was due on the fifth. 'Could you also set a reminder two days before? I'm so tired that I forget everything,' she said. The assistant set the reminder for the third. Meanwhile, a load of washing finished, and Fatima hung it up and went to bed, knowing the bill was in hand.

People want to be reminded to read every night.
Remind me to read tonight
Reading reminder, please
Nudge me at nine to read
Could you remind me every evening at nine? I want to finish this book by September.
I keep falling asleep with a drink in my hand and forgetting my book, so please set a nightly reminder for nine.
Set a daily reading time
I'd like a reminder each night to read, because my eyes need a rest from the screen and a book helps me sleep.

name: spending_ranker
does: Ranks what you spent money on this month from most to least, so you can see which direction to cut, even after a wet month of taxis.
inputs: which month, and which account
people say:
- What did I spend the most on?
- Where does my money go?
- Show me my biggest costs
- What are my top five expenses?
- Which bill is the highest this month?

Chioma, a retired teacher, wanted dinner with her sister. 'Book a table for two at the Thai place at seven,' she told the assistant. A moment later she said, 'Wait, my sister loves Italian. Make it Rosa's instead.' The assistant booked a table for two at Rosa's at seven. Chioma asked, 'Do they have empty tables outside?' The assistant said there were two on the terrace and kept one for them. Chioma smiled and said she could almost taste the pasta already. She told the assistant to remind her at six, and she put a spare fork in her bag, just in case.

People want the phone to read text aloud.
Read this to me
Read it out loud
Can you read my screen?
My eyes are tired, so read the message aloud.
Could you please read the weekly grocery list aloud? I have both hands busy slicing onions and I can't hold the phone.
Speak the text on this page
Please read me the next step of the recipe, since I can't see small print when I'm cooking.
